text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.

-- Alcatel Alsthom chairman Serge Tchuruk says government should reconsider his offer on Thomson as it planned to keep 50 percent of the capital of Thomson unit Thomson Multimedia under French control, and would have paid back to the state any profit made when selling the other 50 percent. The Lagardere offer included handing over Thomson Multimedia to Koorean Daewoo for one symbolic franc, raising wide criticism.
-- Air France Europe launches a domestic shuttle service to Marseille, Nice and Toulouse in move to boost traffic and fend off competition.
-- August foreign exchange figures show historic high surplus of 13.88 billion francs.
-- Credit du Nord CTNTp.PA to buy banque Laydernier from Credit Lyonnais for 77 million francs.
-- Credit Agricole to cut saving and lending rates, Finance Minister Jean Arthuis calls for fair competition in banking sector.
-- Carmaker PSA Peugeot Citroen considering a 3.5 billion francs investment in Brasil's Minas Gerais state.
-- Nouvelles Frontieres travel operator chairman Jacques Maillot reaffirms interest in air traffic, considers bidding for AOM after deciding to withdraw offer for insolvent Air Liberte airline.
-- Daewoo plants in Eastern France allegedly do not meet all safety requirements, workers say French laws on labour are not always observed.
-- Alcatel-CIT to cut about 1,600 jobs from now to end 1998, as part to telecommunications and wiring activity restructuring.
